questions.def: After 'it was', use the verb that logically completes the sentence.
questions.question: It was the novel that ___ her to international fame.

questions.def: 'Only if' requires subject-verb inversion and passive voice.
questions.question: Only ___ the new evidence, would the case be reopened.

questions.def: Passive form emphasizes the action, not the actor.
questions.question: What ___ most is the dedication of the volunteers.

questions.def: 'The fact that' introduces a noun clause as the subject.
questions.question: ___ that the project was a success surprised everyone.

questions.def: 'As' inversion emphasizes the adjective: Rich as he may be.
questions.question: ___ he may be, he lacks the necessary experience.

questions.def: Use past simple for completed action in the past.
questions.question: It ___ that he had already left.

questions.def: 'Not only' requires subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Not only ___ she intelligent, but also incredibly kind.

questions.def: 'Despite' introduces a contrast without a clause.
questions.question: ___ the storm, the ship managed to reach port safely.

questions.def: 'Little' requires subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Little ___ that he was being watched.

questions.def: 'Such...that' emphasizes the degree of something.
questions.question: ___ was her dedication that she won the award.

questions.def: 'Under no circumstances' requires subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Under ___ circumstances should you leave the building.

questions.def: 'Only then' requires subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Only then ___ the danger we were in.

questions.def: 'Seldom' requires subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Seldom ___ such blatant disregard for the rules.

questions.def: 'No sooner...than' is a correlative conjunction.
questions.question: No sooner had we arrived ___ it started to rain.

questions.def: Passive form emphasizes the action, not the actor.
questions.question: It ___ that he was deeply involved.

questions.def: 'In no way' requires subject-verb inversion. Aux. verb 'do'.
questions.question: In no way ___ I condone such behavior.

questions.def: 'Scarcely' requires subject-verb inversion and past perfect.
questions.question: Scarcely ___ the announcement when the crowd cheered.

questions.def: Simple present emphasizes a general truth or feeling.
questions.question: What I ___ most is his honesty.

questions.def: 'Under no circumstances' requires inversion with 'should'.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ this door be opened.

questions.def: 'Hardly' requires subject-verb inversion and past perfect.
questions.question: Hardly ___ the house when it began to rain.

questions.def: 'Little' requires subject-verb inversion and auxiliary verb 'did'.
questions.question: Little ___ they how serious the situation was.

questions.def: 'It was not until then' emphasizes the point of understanding.
questions.question: It was not until ___ that she understood.

questions.def: 'At no time' requires subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: At no time ___ the truth.

questions.def: After requires past perfect for actions completed before another past action.
questions.question: It was only after the negotiations ___ that a resolution was reached.

questions.def: Inversion after 'not only' requires auxiliary verb before the subject.
questions.question: Not only ___ the data accurately, but also presented it clearly.

questions.def: After 'It was', use the subjective pronoun 'they', not 'them'.
questions.question: It was them who leaked the confidential information.

questions.def: In the structure 'What I want to do is + infinitive', use base form.
questions.question: What I want to ___ is the importance of collaboration.

questions.def: Negative adverbials require inversion with auxiliary verb 'should'.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ this door be opened without authorization.

questions.def: Inversion after 'only then' requires auxiliary verb before the subject.
questions.question: Only then ___ the full extent of the damage.

questions.def: Rarely requires subject-auxiliary inversion: 'have I seen'.
questions.question: Rarely I have seen such dedication to a project.
